scope: Second October7 batch; all44 primary subject leaves, all373 generated clinical stable IDs, actual admitted release and selection-only supply. No source excerpts, raw sheet rows or real patient data.

provenance.exactCurriculumMapping: Parent-owned exact ABS/SCORE locator receipt; primary taxonomy counts do not replace it.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Pulmonary optimization before elective incisional-hernia repair
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: For a stable adult with a reducible, nonemergent incisional hernia and poorly controlled COPD, select pulmonary optimization before finalizing elective repair.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial imaging of a palpable breast mass under age 30
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound as the initial imaging study for the scoped adult patient younger than 30 with a new palpable breast mass.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Management of an asymptomatic simple breast cyst
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select no cyst-directed procedure for an imaging-concordant simple breast cyst that is not painful or bothersome.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial treatment of a painful simple breast cyst
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Offer needle aspiration for symptom relief from a persistently painful or bothersome, imaging-concordant simple breast cyst.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Recognition of EBV-associated malignancies
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize canonical EBV-associated malignancies while preserving the boundary that an association is neither universal across every tumor nor an individual cancer-risk prediction.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Apply standard Milan criteria to HCC referral
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Apply standard Milan tumor-number, size, macrovascular-invasion, and extrahepatic-disease criteria to recognize when HCC tumor burden supports transplant-center evaluation without treating the criteria as automatic listing.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Clinical recognition of Mondor disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize the characteristic superficial breast or chest-wall venous cord and its underlying superficial thrombophlebitis.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Selective imaging evaluation of suspected Mondor disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select targeted Doppler ultrasound when the superficial venous diagnosis is uncertain and age-appropriate diagnostic breast imaging when focal symptoms require evaluation for underlying pathology.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Supportive management of uncomplicated Mondor disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Use supportive care for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease while recognizing findings that require renewed evaluation.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Female sex and perioperative mortality after elective AAA repair
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize that women have higher observed perioperative mortality after elective intact AAA repair at the group level, while preserving the boundary that this association does not determine an individual outcome or select a repair approach.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial active surveillance for selected desmoid tumors
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose specialist active surveillance as the initial strategy for newly diagnosed, stable or minimally symptomatic desmoid disease without critical threat or meaningful functional deterioration.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Surgical option for progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize function-preserving resection after multidisciplinary review as an option for progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid when expected morbidity is acceptably low.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy for resectable tail adenocarcinoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select oncologic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy when a fit patient with pancreatic-tail adenocarcinoma has been judged resectable and is proceeding to surgery.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Recognize Felty syndrome
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize Felty syndrome from rheumatoid arthritis with persistent neutropenia, usually with splenomegaly, after important alternative causes have been excluded.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: First-line methotrexate for Felty syndrome
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select specialist-monitored methotrexate as the usual first-line disease-modifying treatment and distinguish bridging therapy from the long-term plan.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Splenectomy for medically refractory Felty syndrome
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Consider splenectomy only after recurrent infections persist despite adequate medical therapy and multidisciplinary review.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Biochemical evaluation for suspected FHH
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Order paired 24-hour urine and serum calcium-creatinine measurements before parathyroid localization when FHH is suspected.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Recognize and confirm FHH
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Use relative hypocalciuria, family context, and appropriate genetic evaluation without treating a low clearance ratio as independently diagnostic.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Avoid unnecessary parathyroid surgery in FHH
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Reassure and observe a patient with confirmed uncomplicated FHH rather than performing routine parathyroid surgery.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Acute lymphangitis clinical recognition
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize acute lymphangitis from a distal skin entry site, a tender erythematous streak extending proximally, and tender regional lymph nodes.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial gallbladder-polyp management category
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select the owner-approved initial management category for a completed incidental gallbladder-polyp ultrasound profile.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Distal cholangiocarcinoma resection selection
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: For the approved resectable distal common-bile-duct profile, select hospital HPB referral for pancreaticoduodenectomy and distinguish the represented distal location.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Obstructive jaundice, vitamin K, and coagulopathy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize the approved relationship between obstructive jaundice, reduced vitamin K absorption, and vitamin K-related coagulopathy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: HCC resection selection in compensated cirrhosis
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: For the approved favorable compensated-cirrhosis profile, select hospital HPB-surgery referral for hepatic resection evaluation without treating Child-Pugh A status or Milan classification alone as sufficient.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Accessory spleen common location
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize the splenic hilum as the most common location represented for an accessory spleen without treating one location as a complete splenectomy plan.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Persistent hemolysis after splenectomy evaluation
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: For the approved persistent-hemolysis presentation after total splenectomy, reassess and evaluate for functioning accessory splenic tissue without relying on MCV, RDW, or Howell-Jolly bodies alone.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Confirmed accessory splenic tissue management
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: For confirmed functioning accessory splenic tissue causing persistent symptomatic hemolysis, refer to hospital surgery for removal without treating incidental tissue as an indication.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Pouchitis after IPAA
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Identify pouchitis as the approved common inflammatory pouch complication after IPAA for ulcerative colitis.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Type IVA congenital bile duct cyst anatomy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Identify Type IVA as the approved combined intrahepatic and extrahepatic cystic-dilatation pattern.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Anal HSIL and high-risk HPV
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Identify high-risk human papillomavirus as the approved etiologic association of anal HSIL.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: MEN2A manifestation pattern
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize the approved MEN2A pattern of medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Pheochromocytoma before thyroid intervention
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize that a functioning pheochromocytoma must be excluded or addressed before thyroid intervention in the approved MEN2A scope.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Alpha blockade before beta blockade
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: When both are indicated for a functioning pheochromocytoma, establish alpha blockade before adding beta blockade.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Endoscopic recognition of colonic lipoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize the characteristic soft, yellowish, deformable subepithelial phenotype of a colonic lipoma while preserving the boundary that an absent cushion sign does not exclude it.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Management of a clearly characterized asymptomatic colonic lipoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose no lipoma-directed treatment or dedicated surveillance for a clearly characterized asymptomatic colonic lipoma and recognize features that make that pathway inapplicable.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Vitamin C in collagen hydroxylation
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Identify vitamin C as a cofactor for proline and lysine hydroxylation in collagen biosynthesis and connect inadequate hydroxylation with reduced collagen stability and impaired healing.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Pathologic recognition of gastric MALT lymphoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize gastric MALT lymphoma from integrated small B-cell morphology, lymphoepithelial lesions, and compatible immunophenotyping while avoiding diagnosis from CD20 alone.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for localized gastric MALT lymphoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for the classic localized low-grade presentation and preserve confirmation and response-reassessment boundaries.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Confirmatory gastric-emptying testing for suspected gastroparesis
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select four-hour solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy to document delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Avoid routine prophylactic splenectomy in proximal gastric cancer
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Preserve the spleen during curative gastrectomy for proximal gastric adenocarcinoma when there is no greater-curvature invasion, direct splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: High-risk peptic-ulcer stigmata requiring endoscopic hemostasis
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Distinguish active spurting, active oozing, and a nonbleeding visible vessel from low-risk clean-base or flat-spot findings when deciding whether endoscopic hemostasis is required.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Endoscopic hemostasis modality selection for peptic-ulcer bleeding
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select an accepted definitive thermal or mechanical modality, recognize that epinephrine is never definitive monotherapy, and apply the conventional epinephrine-plus-definitive-modality pathway without making all monotherapies universally wrong.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Operable distal cholangiocarcinoma tissue evaluation
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: For the approved completed-imaging distal-obstruction profile, select the constrained combined endoscopic tissue-evaluation plan without treating CA 19-9 as confirmation.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Graves clinical-pattern recognition
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize an adult clinical pattern that supports Graves disease: symptoms compatible with thyroid-hormone excess together with diffuse thyroid enlargement and characteristic eye or pretibial skin findings when present, without requiring every feature in every patient.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: TRAb diagnostic support for Graves disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Use TRAb as etiologic support for Graves disease when a patient already has biochemical thyrotoxicosis; distinguish thyroid function from cause and recognize that a negative TRAb result does not fully exclude Graves disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: RAI evaluation for recurrent Graves hyperthyroidism
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize recurrent hyperthyroidism after antithyroid-drug withdrawal as a setting where RAI evaluation is a reasonable counseling option, while retaining surgery and antithyroid-drug treatment as preference-sensitive alternatives.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: RAI contraindication during pregnancy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize current pregnancy as a contraindication to RAI treatment for Graves disease while continuing appropriate endocrine and obstetric assessment without RAI during pregnancy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: RAI contraindication during lactation
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize current breastfeeding as a contraindication to therapeutic iodine-131 for Graves disease and recognize the pre-treatment counseling boundary for feeding the current child.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: RAI avoidance with active moderate-to-severe TED
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Generally avoid therapeutic iodine-131 in ordinary Graves treatment counseling when specialist assessment documents active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial ultrasound for suspected gallstones
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select abdominal ultrasound as the initial imaging study for a stable outpatient with recurrent symptoms compatible with uncomplicated gallstones.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Elective referral for symptomatic gallstones
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Use compatible recurrent symptoms and uncomplicated ultrasound-confirmed gallstones to support elective surgical assessment and cholecystectomy counseling.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Observation of uncomplicated incidental gallstones
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose observation and counseling for uncomplicated incidental gallstones in an asymptomatic adult without suspicious gallbladder features.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Noncontrast CT for unresolved suspected stone disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select noncontrast CT to resolve stone presence, location, and obstruction in a stable nonpregnant adult after indeterminate ultrasound.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Metabolic evaluation after recurrent kidney stones
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select stone analysis when available together with urine and blood metabolic assessment for prevention planning after recurrent confirmed stone disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial serology for suspected celiac disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select tTG-IgA with total-IgA context as a usual initial serologic assessment while a patient with compatible symptoms continues eating gluten.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Usual adult duodenal-biopsy confirmation
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies as the usual confirmation step for an adult with compatible positive celiac serology and adequate IgA.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Dietitian-supported gluten-free treatment
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recommend a gluten-free diet with dietitian support after celiac disease is confirmed in the completed diagnostic pathway.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive FIT
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive screening FIT while recognizing that the stool result alone does not diagnose colorectal cancer.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Histologic confirmation of a colorectal lesion
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Identify histologic examination of sampled lesion tissue as the confirming evidence after colonoscopy identifies a suspicious colorectal lesion.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Iron studies in established anemia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose ferritin and complementary iron studies to determine whether iron deficiency explains established anemia without relying on a numeric threshold.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Gastrointestinal evaluation of unexplained IDA
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recommend suitability assessment for upper endoscopy and colonoscopy in adult men or postmenopausal patients with otherwise unexplained confirmed iron-deficiency anemia.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: MRI characterization of a concerning extremity mass
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select dedicated extremity MRI before biopsy for a deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate soft-tissue mass while recognizing that imaging does not prove sarcoma.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Specialist-planned biopsy of a suspicious soft-tissue mass
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer a suspicious extremity mass to an experienced sarcoma team for planned image-guided core biopsy that preserves the future surgical approach.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: FNA selection for a suspicious thyroid nodule
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select ultrasound-guided FNA after normal TSH and ultrasound findings meeting biopsy criteria in the scoped stable outpatient pathway.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Follicular invasion requires histology
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize that capsular or vascular invasion distinguishing follicular adenoma from carcinoma requires histologic evaluation rather than follicular cytology alone.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Biochemical confirmation of primary hyperparathyroidism
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Use repeat serum calcium with intact PTH to establish the biochemical pattern before localization planning in the scoped stable outpatient pathway.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Surgical assessment for complicated primary hyperparathyroidism
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recommend parathyroid surgical assessment for biochemically confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism with authored renal or skeletal complications.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Dynamic ultrasound after an equivocal inguinal-hernia examination
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select targeted dynamic groin ultrasound for the scoped stable patient with intermittent symptoms and an equivocal examination.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Elective planning for symptomatic inguinal hernia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recommend elective repair discussion and planning after a reducible inguinal hernia is confirmed in a patient with meaningful activity-limiting symptoms.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Clinical recognition of acute anal fissure
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize an uncomplicated acute anal fissure from recent defecation-related pain, scant bleeding, and a superficial midline tear.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial conservative care for acute anal fissure
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select stool-regulating fiber, fluids, soft formed stools, and sitz baths as initial care for a typical uncomplicated acute fissure.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Anoscopy for suspected internal hemorrhoids
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select anoscopy to define local canal anatomy after an appropriate broader evaluation in a stable patient with suspected internal hemorrhoids.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Office banding for persistent internal hemorrhoids
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select office rubber-band ligation for uncomplicated bleeding or prolapsing internal hemorrhoids that persist after conservative care.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Upper endoscopy for persistent esophageal dysphagia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select upper-GI endoscopy with appropriate esophageal biopsies for stable persistent esophageal dysphagia with a structural or mucosal concern.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Barrett esophagus on esophageal biopsy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize Barrett esophagus from a sampled columnar esophageal segment with specialized intestinal metaplasia.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: High-resolution manometry for suspected achalasia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select high-resolution esophageal manometry after adequate structural evaluation for persistent solids-and-liquids dysphagia with regurgitation.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Manometric recognition of achalasia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize achalasia from absent peristalsis and impaired esophagogastric-junction relaxation without relying on an unsupported numeric threshold.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Complete diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious pigmented lesion
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select complete diagnostic excision with narrow margins and adequate depth for a small accessible pigmented lesion concerning for melanoma.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Sentinel-node staging discussion for melanoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Discuss sentinel lymph-node biopsy for pathological regional staging of intermediate-thickness clinically node-negative melanoma alongside definitive excision planning.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Ultrasound characterization of postoperative fullness
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select targeted ultrasound to characterize an uncertain superficial collection after benign breast excision.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Observation of an uncomplicated postoperative seroma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Observe a small simple asymptomatic postoperative seroma without infection, wound tension, implant, or functional limitation.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Clinical recognition of chronic pilonidal sinus
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize chronic pilonidal sinus disease from recurrent natal-cleft drainage and characteristic midline pits without a current abscess.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Off-midline closure planning for pilonidal disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Plan an off-midline closure when excision with primary closure has already been selected for chronic pilonidal disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Targeted ultrasound for suspected lactational breast abscess
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound for a persistent focal inflammatory breast mass during lactation.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Selected drainage of a lactational breast abscess
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose image-guided drainage with culture and individualized antibiotic care for a suitable uncomplicated lactational abscess while preserving feeding when contact precautions are met.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Laryngeal examination after thyroid surgery
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select laryngeal visualization for persistent voice change after thyroid surgery.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: External superior laryngeal nerve localization
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Localize loss of high pitch and projection with preserved ordinary vocal-fold mobility to external superior laryngeal nerve and cricothyroid dysfunction.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Contrast swallow for suspected Zenker diverticulum
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select contrast swallow with fluoroscopy for a classic proximal pouch presentation.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Zenker false-pouch anatomy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize a posterior mucosa-and-submucosa pouch above the cricopharyngeus as Zenker anatomy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Resting ABI for suspected peripheral arterial disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select resting ankle-brachial index testing for classic stable claudication symptoms and examination findings.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Structured exercise for stable claudication
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select supervised or structured exercise before invasive therapy for stable functionally limiting claudication after risk reduction is addressed.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Three-site skeletal assessment in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select lumbar-spine, hip, and distal forearm DXA for skeletal assessment after primary hyperparathyroidism is confirmed.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Age-based surgical assessment in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize age under 50 years as an independent reason to discuss parathyroid surgery after confirmed asymptomatic disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: ACTH classification after confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select plasma ACTH to classify the cause after endogenous hypercortisolism is already confirmed.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Adrenal imaging after suppressed ACTH
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select adrenal imaging for the suppressed-ACTH branch of confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: MRCP duct assessment for an indeterminate pancreatic cyst
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Use MRI/MRCP to assess communication between an indeterminate pancreatic cyst and the main duct.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: MCN-compatible pancreatic-cyst pattern recognition
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize a body or tail cyst without main-duct communication as MCN-compatible without claiming definitive histology or automatic resection.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Preoperative cross-sectional staging for colon cancer
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis before treatment planning for confirmed colon cancer.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Oncologic regional resection for colon cancer
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select resection of the tumor-bearing colon with its regional lymphatic drainage for localized resectable colon cancer.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Multimodal response assessment after rectal cancer treatment
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select combined digital rectal examination, endoscopy, and rectal-protocol MRI after neoadjuvant treatment.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Selected watch-and-wait after clinical complete response
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize intensive-surveillance watch-and-wait as an acceptable nonsurgical option for a fully informed adherent patient with a clinical complete response in an experienced program.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Confirmatory vascular imaging after carotid duplex
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select confirmatory CT angiography after duplex suggests severe symptomatic carotid stenosis.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Endarterectomy assessment for severe symptomatic carotid stenosis
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select prompt carotid endarterectomy assessment with best medical therapy for a suitable patient with severe ipsilateral symptomatic stenosis.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Germline polyposis evaluation after diffuse adenomas
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select hereditary counseling and APC/MUTYH germline testing after colonoscopy establishes diffuse adenomatous polyposis.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: IPAA referral for uncontrolled rectal FAP burden
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select restorative proctocolectomy/IPAA referral when rectal adenomas cannot be controlled endoscopically and restoration is appropriate.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: MRI mapping for recurrent complex fistula
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select pelvic MRI to map recurrent complex fistula anatomy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Sphincter-preserving staged planning for high fistula
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose loose-seton referral and staged sphincter-preserving planning for high transsphincteric anatomy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Colonoscopy after recovered complicated diverticulitis
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select colonoscopy after first recovered complicated diverticulitis without recent adequate examination.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Individualized elective sigmoid discussion
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Discuss elective sigmoid resection using recovery burden and patient context rather than episode count.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Biopsy with CT and MRI staging of an anal-canal lesion
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Arrange tissue biopsy with CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and pelvic MRI for a suspicious anal-canal lesion.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Chemoradiation referral for localized anal-canal SCC
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer nonmetastatic anal-canal SCC after CT and pelvic MRI for definitive chemoradiation planning.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Venous duplex for suspected postoperative DVT
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select prompt venous duplex/compression ultrasound for new unilateral postoperative leg symptoms.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Finite anticoagulation after surgery-provoked DVT
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select finite anticoagulation planning for a first uncomplicated major-surgery-provoked proximal DVT when safe.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: HIV and hepatitis-C evaluation in presumed ITP
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select HIV and hepatitis-C testing before concluding primary ITP in compatible isolated thrombocytopenia.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Deferring elective splenectomy in persistent ITP
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Defer elective splenectomy when feasible in stable persistent ITP of only several months.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: EUS core and molecular evaluation of selected gastric GIST
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select EUS-guided core tissue and molecular testing when a challenging gastric mass may receive preoperative targeted therapy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Mutation-guided neoadjuvant planning for challenging GIST
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select neoadjuvant imatinib only for an imatinib-sensitive GIST when shrinkage is expected to reduce operative morbidity.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Multiphasic MRI characterization of hepatic adenoma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select multiphasic liver MRI to characterize a suspected hepatic adenoma while respecting imaging limitations.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Resection planning for hepatic adenoma in men
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer a stable man with a characterized hepatic adenoma for elective resection planning regardless of lesion size.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: CTA evaluation of chronic mesenteric ischemia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select mesenteric CTA for compatible chronic postprandial symptoms after reasonable exclusion of alternatives.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Revascularization referral for symptomatic multivessel CMI
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer symptomatic multivessel occlusive chronic mesenteric ischemia for expert revascularization planning.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Prepared ARR screening for primary aldosteronism
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select aldosterone and renin testing with ARR after potassium and medication preparation in resistant hypertension with spontaneous hypokalemia.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: CT and AVS before lateralized adrenal surgery
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select adrenal CT plus AVS before deciding unilateral surgery in an appropriate adult with confirmed primary aldosteronism.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: MRCP for an intermediate-risk duct stone
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select MRCP for stable intermediate-likelihood choledocholithiasis when the local route favors noninvasive imaging.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Therapeutic ERCP referral for a confirmed duct stone
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer a confirmed duct stone for therapeutic ERCP when the selected local pathway clears the duct before cholecystectomy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Hepatobiliary-contrast MRCP for bile-leak anatomy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select hepatobiliary-contrast MRCP after CT to localize a stable postoperative bile leak and assess duct continuity.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: ERCP stent referral for a persistent minor bile leak
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer a persistent minor leak with preserved duct continuity for ERCP and plastic-stent treatment.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Contrast CT characterization of a pancreatic fluid collection
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Order contrast-enhanced CT before classifying or planning drainage of a symptomatic post-pancreatitis collection.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Endoscopic drainage referral for a symptomatic pseudocyst
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize mature pseudocyst morphology on returned CT and refer a symptomatic suitably apposed collection for EUS-guided drainage.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Off-PPI reflux monitoring for unproven GERD
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Order ambulatory reflux monitoring off PPI when normal endoscopy leaves GERD unproven before invasive therapy.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: High-resolution manometry before antireflux planning
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Order high-resolution manometry after objective reflux confirmation and before operative planning.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Completed Whipple triad in post-bariatric hypoglycemia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Recognize PBH when a spontaneous episode already documents symptoms, venous plasma hypoglycemia, and relief after correction.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Initial dietary care for post-bariatric hypoglycemia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Start specialist dietitian-led individualized dietary care for stable confirmed PBH.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Tumor MMR screening in colorectal cancer
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select tumor MMR IHC screening for a newly diagnosed colorectal cancer in the local universal-screening pathway.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Genetics counseling after suggestive tumor IHC
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Refer a Lynch-suggestive MSH2/MSH6-loss tumor result for genetics counseling and germline-testing discussion.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Topical CCB for chronic anal fissure
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select topical CCB as the local first-line pharmacologic treatment for typical chronic anal fissure.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Selected LIS discussion after chronic-fissure medical treatment
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Discuss LIS after failed medical treatment for selected chronic anal fissure without described continence risk.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious keratinocyte lesion
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select adequate diagnostic biopsy for a suspicious lesion before cSCC risk-directed treatment.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Risk-directed surgery for cutaneous SCC
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Choose standard excision for low-risk cSCC and Mohs-capable referral for high-risk cSCC.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Arterial assessment before venous-ulcer compression
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Obtain arterial assessment before selecting compression for a suspected venous leg ulcer.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Compression after adequate arterial assessment
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select compression therapy for a stable venous leg ulcer after returned arterial assessment supports its use.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Vaccine review before elective splenectomy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Review indicated encapsulated-organism vaccines before elective splenectomy and coordinate them at least 14 days before surgery when possible.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Emergency action for fever with asplenia
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select immediate emergency assessment for a known asplenic patient with fever without outpatient test delay.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Cortisol screening for adrenal incidentaloma
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test to evaluate autonomous cortisol secretion in a stable adult with an adrenal incidentaloma.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Pheochromocytoma exclusion before adrenal biopsy
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Exclude pheochromocytoma biochemically before considering a management-changing biopsy of an indeterminate adrenal mass.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Full-thickness biopsy for suspected mammary Paget disease
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Select full-thickness nipple-areolar skin biopsy for persistent unilateral changes suspicious for mammary Paget disease.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Underlying breast evaluation after mammary Paget diagnosis
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Evaluate for underlying breast carcinoma with mammography and ultrasound after mammary Paget disease is confirmed.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Tissue confirmation of inflammatory breast cancer
activeBaselineMappings.learningObjective: Arrange breast core biopsy and staging for a rapid diffuse inflammatory breast presentation without an abscess.

activeBaselineMappings.displayName: Neoadjuvant sequence for stage III inflammatory breast cancer

addedObjectives.displayName: Localize median compression at the wrist

addedObjectives.displayName: Localize ulnar compression at the elbow
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Use supplied little/ring-finger symptoms and elbow provocation to localize cubital-tunnel compression to the ulnar nerve at the elbow.

addedObjectives.displayName: Evaluate a persistent adult neck mass
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Continue malignancy evaluation of a persistent adult lateral/cystic mass with an appropriate selected contrast-enhanced neck CT, without reassurance from cystic appearance.

addedObjectives.displayName: Refer for initial needle sampling of a neck mass
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Choose specialist fine-needle aspiration as the best offered initial needle approach for an assessed at-risk adult neck mass rather than initial open biopsy.

addedObjectives.displayName: Distinguish a graft from a flap by blood supply
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Classify supplied reconstructive tissue transfers by whether blood supply is retained or carried and reconnected, rather than by donor identity or location.

addedObjectives.displayName: Explain epithelial regrowth at a split-thickness donor site
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Explain how retained donor-site skin appendage epithelium contributes to resurfacing after a split-thickness harvest, separately from recipient-graft vascularization.

addedObjectives.displayName: Classify graft donor relationships
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Classify an autograft, allograft, isograft or xenograft from the supplied donor-recipient relationship.

addedObjectives.displayName: Explain local-anesthetic nerve blockade
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Identify voltage-gated sodium-channel blockade as the principal mechanism interrupting sensory nerve excitation and conduction.

addedObjectives.displayName: Explain tacrolimus immunosuppression
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Identify the FKBP12–calcineurin pathway and suppression of T-cell activation underlying tacrolimus immunosuppression.

addedObjectives.displayName: Distinguish paralysis from anesthesia
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Recognize that neuromuscular blockade produces skeletal-muscle relaxation without itself providing unconsciousness or analgesia.

addedObjectives.displayName: Recognize systemic local-anesthetic toxicity
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Recognize a compatible neurologic or cardiac toxicity pattern after supplied local-anesthetic exposure in a completed outside-care event.

addedObjectives.displayName: Explain refeeding-related phosphate shifts
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Explain how carbohydrate-associated insulin and the return to anabolic metabolism can lower serum phosphate through cellular uptake in a compatible refeeding course.

addedObjectives.displayName: Plan thiamine in high-risk nutrition restart
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Recognize planned thiamine before a specialist-monitored high-risk nutrition restart, while retaining separate electrolyte and clinical monitoring.

addedObjectives.displayName: Match RCA and FMEA to the safety task
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Distinguish retrospective event-centered root cause analysis from prospective process-centered healthcare failure mode and effects analysis.

addedObjectives.displayName: Distinguish saturation from oxygen content
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Explain why a normal oxygen saturation does not establish adequate hemoglobin-dependent oxygen content or exclude supplied anemia.

addedObjectives.displayName: Attribute bowel melanoma to its confirmed skin primary
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Use a supplied cutaneous primary and confirmatory outside pathology to identify small-bowel melanoma as metastatic disease retaining the primary cancer's identity.

addedObjectives.displayName: Interpret negative films after swallowing a bone
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Recognize that negative plain films and preserved breathing do not exclude a retained swallowed bone in a symptomatic esophageal context.

addedObjectives.displayName: Refer confirmed sharp esophageal objects emergently
addedObjectives.learningObjective: Arrange emergency hospital therapeutic endoscopic care for a confirmed sharp esophageal foreign body rather than elective observation or routine clinic scheduling.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Female sex and perioperative mortality after elective AAA repair
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize that women have higher observed perioperative mortality after elective intact AAA repair at the group level, while preserving the boundary that this association does not determine an individual outcome or select a repair approach.
Select one-time abdominal ultrasound screening for a man age 65-75 who has ever smoked.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Elective repair evaluation for a 6-cm AAA
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer an acceptable-risk patient with an asymptomatic 6-cm fusiform AAA for elective vascular repair evaluation.
Avoid routine abscess incision when examination shows diffuse nonpurulent inflammation without a focal collection.
Recognize rapid or extensive spread as exceeding the uncomplicated clinic abscess pathway.
Recognize the splenic hilum as the most common location represented for an accessory spleen without treating one location as a complete splenectomy plan.
Select high-resolution esophageal manometry after adequate structural evaluation for persistent solids-and-liquids dysphagia with regurgitation.
Recognize achalasia from absent peristalsis and impaired esophagogastric-junction relaxation without relying on an unsupported numeric threshold.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Immediate care for acute limb ischemia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Begin unfractionated heparin unless contraindicated and arrange emergency vascular care or transfer for acute limb ischemia.
Classify acute limb ischemia as viable, marginally threatened, immediately threatened, or irreversible using complete sensory, motor, arterial Doppler, and venous Doppler findings.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Immediate exploration for mesenteric ischemia with peritonitis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Send suspected acute mesenteric ischemia with overt peritonitis for immediate operative exploration without further diagnostic delay.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Prompt CTA for acute mesenteric ischemia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Transfer for CTA without delay when acute mesenteric ischemia is suspected, including when acute kidney injury is present.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Cholecystectomy before discharge after mild biliary pancreatitis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Arrange index-admission cholecystectomy before discharge after mild gallstone pancreatitis when the patient is clinically appropriate.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Selective CT in mild acute pancreatitis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Avoid routine early CT when mild acute pancreatitis is clinically established and improving, while reserving CT for uncertainty or failure to improve.
Select a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test to evaluate autonomous cortisol secretion in a stable adult with an adrenal incidentaloma.
Exclude pheochromocytoma biochemically before considering a management-changing biopsy of an indeterminate adrenal mass.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Clinical recognition of acute anal fissure
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize an uncomplicated acute anal fissure from recent defecation-related pain, scant bleeding, and a superficial midline tear.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial conservative care for acute anal fissure
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select stool-regulating fiber, fluids, soft formed stools, and sitz baths as initial care for a typical uncomplicated acute fissure.
Identify high-risk human papillomavirus as the approved etiologic association of anal HSIL.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Biopsy with CT and MRI staging of an anal-canal lesion
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Arrange tissue biopsy with CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and pelvic MRI for a suspicious anal-canal lesion.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Chemoradiation referral for localized anal-canal SCC
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer nonmetastatic anal-canal SCC after CT and pelvic MRI for definitive chemoradiation planning.
Recognize an appendicolith as a risk modifier that favors operative hospital care over a routine antibiotics-only pathway while preserving shared decision-making.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Urgent disposition for a classic appendicitis pattern
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select prompt emergency-department evaluation for a stable outpatient with a classic concerning appendicitis presentation.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognition of an incomplete appendicitis pattern
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Maintain suspicion for appendicitis when progressive focal right-lower-quadrant findings are present despite an incomplete classic pattern.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Do not delay suspected appendicitis for unavailable testing
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose emergency-department transfer rather than delaying a concerning appendicitis presentation for unavailable CT or substituting plain X-ray.
Select CT for a stable nonpregnant adult with persistent appendicitis concern after nondiagnostic ultrasound when timely MRI is unavailable.
Identify increased alveolar-capillary permeability as the core mechanism of inflammatory pulmonary edema in ARDS.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Predicted body weight for ARDS ventilation
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use predicted body weight, not fluctuating actual weight, as the body-weight basis for ARDS tidal-volume selection.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Emergency action for fever with asplenia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select immediate emergency assessment for a known asplenic patient with fever without outpatient test delay.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Age-based surgical assessment in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize age under 50 years as an independent reason to discuss parathyroid surgery after confirmed asymptomatic disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Three-site skeletal assessment in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select lumbar-spine, hip, and distal forearm DXA for skeletal assessment after primary hyperparathyroidism is confirmed.
Recognize Barrett esophagus from a sampled columnar esophageal segment with specialized intestinal metaplasia.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognize a basal cell carcinoma pattern
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize clinical patterns concerning for BCC and arrange diagnostic confirmation.
Explain that local destruction is the principal concern and metastasis is rare without minimizing advanced disease.
Select hepatobiliary-contrast MRCP after CT to localize a stable postoperative bile leak and assess duct continuity.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: ERCP stent referral for a persistent minor bile leak
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer a persistent minor leak with preserved duct continuity for ERCP and plastic-stent treatment.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: ECG and troponin evaluation for blunt cardiac injury
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer a clinic arrival with concerning blunt chest trauma for emergency evaluation that includes ECG and cardiac troponin rather than relying on ECG alone.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Monitored disposition after blunt cardiac injury screening
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use completed ECG and troponin results to select monitored hospital care for either abnormal result and recognize the normal-both boundary.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Select breast conservation after neoadjuvant therapy
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize selected noninflammatory breast cancers that remain eligible for breast conservation after response.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Map breast cancer response after neoadjuvant therapy
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Integrate baseline and post-treatment breast/axillary findings and localization into operative mapping.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Management of an asymptomatic simple breast cyst
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select no cyst-directed procedure for an imaging-concordant simple breast cyst that is not painful or bothersome.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial treatment of a painful simple breast cyst
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Offer needle aspiration for symptom relief from a persistently painful or bothersome, imaging-concordant simple breast cyst.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognition of suspicious mammographic calcification patterns
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Distinguish suspicious calcification morphology and distribution from typically benign patterns without treating any isolated descriptor as a tissue diagnosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognition of suspicious mammographic mass morphology
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize mass shape and margin combinations that are concerning on mammography while preserving the boundary that imaging morphology is not a tissue diagnosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial diagnostic imaging of a palpable breast mass at age 30 to 39
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis with targeted breast ultrasound for the scoped patient age 30 to 39 with a new palpable breast mass.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Core biopsy of a suspicious solid breast mass
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select image-guided core biopsy for an accessible solid breast mass categorized as suspicious on diagnostic imaging.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial imaging of a palpable breast mass under age 30
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound as the initial imaging study for the scoped adult patient younger than 30 with a new palpable breast mass.
Use burn and patient factors to select outpatient reassessment, consultation, or emergency transfer.
Distinguish superficial partial-thickness from deeper thermal burns using wound findings.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Confirmatory vascular imaging after carotid duplex
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select confirmatory CT angiography after duplex suggests severe symptomatic carotid stenosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Endarterectomy assessment for severe symptomatic carotid stenosis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select prompt carotid endarterectomy assessment with best medical therapy for a suitable patient with severe ipsilateral symptomatic stenosis.
Select upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies as the usual confirmation step for an adult with compatible positive celiac serology and adequate IgA.
Recommend a gluten-free diet with dietitian support after celiac disease is confirmed in the completed diagnostic pathway.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial serology for suspected celiac disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select tTG-IgA with total-IgA context as a usual initial serologic assessment while a patient with compatible symptoms continues eating gluten.
Send a fit patient with confirmed acute calculous cholecystitis for hospital care and index-admission laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Select hepatobiliary scintigraphy to clarify suspected acute cholecystitis after equivocal ultrasound when another study is needed and available.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Type IVA congenital bile duct cyst anatomy
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify Type IVA as the approved combined intrahepatic and extrahepatic cystic-dilatation pattern.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Therapeutic ERCP referral for a confirmed duct stone
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer a confirmed duct stone for therapeutic ERCP when the selected local pathway clears the duct before cholecystectomy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: MRCP for an intermediate-risk duct stone
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select MRCP for stable intermediate-likelihood choledocholithiasis when the local route favors noninvasive imaging.
Distinguish stable biliary symptoms from warning features requiring emergency evaluation.
Arrange formal ultrasound-based evaluation for stable suspected gallstone disease without substituting plain radiography.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Selected LIS discussion after chronic-fissure medical treatment
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Discuss LIS after failed medical treatment for selected chronic anal fissure without described continence risk.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Topical CCB for chronic anal fissure
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select topical CCB as the local first-line pharmacologic treatment for typical chronic anal fissure.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: CTA evaluation of chronic mesenteric ischemia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select mesenteric CTA for compatible chronic postprandial symptoms after reasonable exclusion of alternatives.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Revascularization referral for symptomatic multivessel CMI
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer symptomatic multivessel occlusive chronic mesenteric ischemia for expert revascularization planning.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Fluid confirmation of suspected chylous ascites
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Confirm suspected chylous ascites through diagnostic fluid sampling rather than inferring fluid composition from CT appearance.
Pause a nonurgent elective plan for case-specific multidisciplinary optimization when active decompensation is present.
Use multidimensional liver, patient, procedure, and facility factors in perioperative cirrhosis assessment.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Choose a conditional aPTT mixing assessment
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select a specialist mixing study as an initial deficiency-versus-inhibition assessment for a repeated unexplained isolated prolonged aPTT when immediate FVIII:C is unavailable and interferences have been assessed.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Interpret a mixing study as an initial clue
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Interpret correction, noncorrection and time-dependent changes as initial laboratory clues while preserving method limitations and the need for factor/inhibitor assessment.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Oncologic regional resection for colon cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select resection of the tumor-bearing colon with its regional lymphatic drainage for localized resectable colon cancer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Preoperative cross-sectional staging for colon cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis before treatment planning for confirmed colon cancer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Management of a clearly characterized asymptomatic colonic lipoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose no lipoma-directed treatment or dedicated surveillance for a clearly characterized asymptomatic colonic lipoma and recognize features that make that pathway inapplicable.
Recognize the characteristic soft, yellowish, deformable subepithelial phenotype of a colonic lipoma while preserving the boundary that an absent cushion sign does not exclude it.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Histologic confirmation of a colorectal lesion
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify histologic examination of sampled lesion tissue as the confirming evidence after colonoscopy identifies a suspicious colorectal lesion.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive FIT
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive screening FIT while recognizing that the stool result alone does not diagnose colorectal cancer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Sphincter-preserving staged planning for high fistula
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose loose-seton referral and staged sphincter-preserving planning for high transsphincteric anatomy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: MRI mapping for recurrent complex fistula
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select pelvic MRI to map recurrent complex fistula anatomy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: ACTH classification after confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select plasma ACTH to classify the cause after endogenous hypercortisolism is already confirmed.
Select adrenal imaging for the suppressed-ACTH branch of confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome.
Select targeted soft-tissue ultrasound when examination cannot distinguish cellulitis from an abscess.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Drainage of a confirmed cutaneous abscess
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select incision and drainage as primary treatment for a confirmed uncomplicated cutaneous abscess.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious keratinocyte lesion
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select adequate diagnostic biopsy for a suspicious lesion before cSCC risk-directed treatment.
Choose standard excision for low-risk cSCC and Mohs-capable referral for high-risk cSCC.
Apply the 2-mm standard and individualize narrower negative margins for pure DCIS treated with breast conservation and whole-breast irradiation.
Use the planned breast operation, future mapping, and invasion concern to decide whether DCIS requires sentinel-node staging.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial active surveillance for selected desmoid tumors
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose specialist active surveillance as the initial strategy for newly diagnosed, stable or minimally symptomatic desmoid disease without critical threat or meaningful functional deterioration.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Surgical option for progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize function-preserving resection after multidisciplinary review as an option for progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid when expected morbidity is acceptably low.
Distinguish clinical infection from colonization and escalate danger features externally.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Avoid antibiotics for uninfected diabetic foot ulcer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Withhold antibiotics used solely for prevention or healing when clinical infection is absent.
Recognize clinical or dialysis-performance dysfunction and refer to the access team.
Use look, feel, and listen examination and external specialist ultrasound when maturation remains uncertain.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Avoid calorie overfeeding in kidney disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Avoid excess calories intended only to force positive nitrogen balance during kidney-disease nutrition support.
Apply the hospitalized conventional-dialysis protein target in the absence of acute or critical illness without extending it to outpatient or critical-care populations.
Plan lobectomy versus total thyroidectomy from disease extent and patient goals rather than one blanket rule.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Map DTC with preoperative neck ultrasound
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select central and lateral neck ultrasonography after malignant thyroid cytology or molecular findings.
For the approved completed-imaging distal-obstruction profile, select the constrained combined endoscopic tissue-evaluation plan without treating CA 19-9 as confirmation.
For the approved resectable distal common-bile-duct profile, select hospital HPB referral for pancreaticoduodenectomy and distinguish the represented distal location.
Select CT to confirm a first suspected diverticulitis presentation and assess for complications.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Selected supportive care for uncomplicated diverticulitis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use outpatient supportive care without routine antibiotics for a carefully selected mild uncomplicated case.
Recognize canonical EBV-associated malignancies while preserving the boundary that an association is neither universal across every tumor nor an individual cancer-risk prediction.
Review indicated encapsulated-organism vaccines before elective splenectomy and coordinate them at least 14 days before surgery when possible.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Dilation with anti-inflammatory care for fibrostenotic EoE
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Plan dilation together with anti-inflammatory care for symptomatic fibrostenotic eosinophilic esophagitis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Multilevel esophageal biopsies for suspected EoE
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select upper endoscopy with adequate multilevel biopsies for suspected eosinophilic esophagitis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Upper endoscopy for persistent esophageal dysphagia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select upper-GI endoscopy with appropriate esophageal biopsies for stable persistent esophageal dysphagia with a structural or mucosal concern.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Germline polyposis evaluation after diffuse adenomas
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select hereditary counseling and APC/MUTYH germline testing after colonoscopy establishes diffuse adenomatous polyposis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: IPAA referral for uncontrolled rectal FAP burden
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select restorative proctocolectomy/IPAA referral when rectal adenomas cannot be controlled endoscopically and restoration is appropriate.
Protect exposed bowel with a sterile moist covering and activate immediate emergency surgical transfer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Endoanal ultrasound for sphincter repair planning
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select endoanal ultrasound when sphincter anatomy is needed for possible repair planning.
Begin stable fecal incontinence care with dietary and medical measures tailored to stool consistency and bowel habits.
Select specialist-monitored methotrexate as the usual first-line disease-modifying treatment and distinguish bridging therapy from the long-term plan.
Recognize Felty syndrome from rheumatoid arthritis with persistent neutropenia, usually with splenomegaly, after important alternative causes have been excluded.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Splenectomy for medically refractory Felty syndrome
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Consider splenectomy only after recurrent infections persist despite adequate medical therapy and multidisciplinary review.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Timely elective repair planning for femoral hernia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Arrange timely elective repair evaluation for a stable reducible femoral hernia.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Avoid unnecessary parathyroid surgery in FHH
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Reassure and observe a patient with confirmed uncomplicated FHH rather than performing routine parathyroid surgery.
Order paired 24-hour urine and serum calcium-creatinine measurements before parathyroid localization when FHH is suspected.
Use relative hypocalciuria, family context, and appropriate genetic evaluation without treating a low clearance ratio as independently diagnostic.
Avoid routine excision of an asymptomatic concordant core-proven fibroadenoma without atypia or phyllodes concern.
Select the owner-approved initial management category for a completed incidental gallbladder-polyp ultrasound profile.
Choose observation and counseling for uncomplicated incidental gallstones in an asymptomatic adult without suspicious gallbladder features.
Select abdominal ultrasound as the initial imaging study for a stable outpatient with recurrent symptoms compatible with uncomplicated gallstones.
Use compatible recurrent symptoms and uncomplicated ultrasound-confirmed gallstones to support elective surgical assessment and cholecystectomy counseling.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Avoid routine prophylactic splenectomy in proximal gastric cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Preserve the spleen during curative gastrectomy for proximal gastric adenocarcinoma when there is no greater-curvature invasion, direct splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: EUS core and molecular evaluation of selected gastric GIST
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select EUS-guided core tissue and molecular testing when a challenging gastric mass may receive preoperative targeted therapy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Mutation-guided neoadjuvant planning for challenging GIST
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select neoadjuvant imatinib only for an imatinib-sensitive GIST when shrinkage is expected to reduce operative morbidity.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for localized gastric MALT lymphoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for the classic localized low-grade presentation and preserve confirmation and response-reassessment boundaries.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Pathologic recognition of gastric MALT lymphoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize gastric MALT lymphoma from integrated small B-cell morphology, lymphoepithelial lesions, and compatible immunophenotyping while avoiding diagnosis from CD20 alone.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Confirmatory gastric-emptying testing for suspected gastroparesis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select four-hour solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy to document delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
Map documented eye, verbal, and motor responses and sum only when all are testable.
Record V-NT with its reason and avoid a misleading numeric total.
Order high-resolution manometry after objective reflux confirmation and before operative planning.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Off-PPI reflux monitoring for unproven GERD
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Order ambulatory reflux monitoring off PPI when normal endoscopy leaves GERD unproven before invasive therapy.

Recognize an adult clinical pattern that supports Graves disease: symptoms compatible with thyroid-hormone excess together with diffuse thyroid enlargement and characteristic eye or pretibial skin findings when present, without requiring every feature in every patient.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: RAI avoidance with active moderate-to-severe TED
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Generally avoid therapeutic iodine-131 in ordinary Graves treatment counseling when specialist assessment documents active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: RAI evaluation for recurrent Graves hyperthyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize recurrent hyperthyroidism after antithyroid-drug withdrawal as a setting where RAI evaluation is a reasonable counseling option, while retaining surgery and antithyroid-drug treatment as preference-sensitive alternatives.
Recognize current breastfeeding as a contraindication to therapeutic iodine-131 for Graves disease and recognize the pre-treatment counseling boundary for feeding the current child.
Recognize current pregnancy as a contraindication to RAI treatment for Graves disease while continuing appropriate endocrine and obstetric assessment without RAI during pregnancy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: TRAb diagnostic support for Graves disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use TRAb as etiologic support for Graves disease when a patient already has biochemical thyrotoxicosis; distinguish thyroid function from cause and recognize that a negative TRAb result does not fully exclude Graves disease.
Recognize a compatible neurologic or cardiac toxicity pattern after supplied local-anesthetic exposure in a completed outside-care event.
Recognize that neuromuscular blockade produces skeletal-muscle relaxation without itself providing unconsciousness or analgesia.
Explain why a normal oxygen saturation does not establish adequate hemoglobin-dependent oxygen content or exclude supplied anemia.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Refer confirmed sharp esophageal objects emergently
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Arrange emergency hospital therapeutic endoscopic care for a confirmed sharp esophageal foreign body rather than elective observation or routine clinic scheduling.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Interpret negative films after swallowing a bone
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize that negative plain films and preserved breathing do not exclude a retained swallowed bone in a symptomatic esophageal context.
Select pregnancy hCG testing during assessment of reproductive-age pelvic or abdominal pain when pregnancy is possible.
Recognize symptomatic possible ectopic pregnancy and arrange urgent specialist-capable assessment despite initial hemodynamic stability.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Refer for initial needle sampling of a neck mass
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose specialist fine-needle aspiration as the best offered initial needle approach for an assessed at-risk adult neck mass rather than initial open biopsy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Evaluate a persistent adult neck mass
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Continue malignancy evaluation of a persistent adult lateral/cystic mass with an appropriate selected contrast-enhanced neck CT, without reassurance from cystic appearance.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Plan thiamine in high-risk nutrition restart
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize planned thiamine before a specialist-monitored high-risk nutrition restart, while retaining separate electrolyte and clinical monitoring.
Explain how carbohydrate-associated insulin and the return to anabolic metabolism can lower serum phosphate through cellular uptake in a compatible refeeding course.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Attribute bowel melanoma to its confirmed skin primary
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use a supplied cutaneous primary and confirmatory outside pathology to identify small-bowel melanoma as metastatic disease retaining the primary cancer's identity.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Match RCA and FMEA to the safety task
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Distinguish retrospective event-centered root cause analysis from prospective process-centered healthcare failure mode and effects analysis.
Identify voltage-gated sodium-channel blockade as the principal mechanism interrupting sensory nerve excitation and conduction.
Identify the FKBP12–calcineurin pathway and suppression of T-cell activation underlying tacrolimus immunosuppression.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Distinguish a graft from a flap by blood supply
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Classify supplied reconstructive tissue transfers by whether blood supply is retained or carried and reconnected, rather than by donor identity or location.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Localize median compression at the wrist
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use supplied sensory distribution and wrist findings to localize a carpal-tunnel pattern to the median nerve at the wrist.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Explain how retained donor-site skin appendage epithelium contributes to resurfacing after a split-thickness harvest, separately from recipient-graft vascularization.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Localize ulnar compression at the elbow
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use supplied little/ring-finger symptoms and elbow provocation to localize cubital-tunnel compression to the ulnar nerve at the elbow.
Classify an autograft, allograft, isograft or xenograft from the supplied donor-recipient relationship.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Active H. pylori testing for duodenal ulcer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select a nonserologic active-infection test for H. pylori in uncomplicated duodenal ulcer disease.
Plan nonserologic confirmation of H. pylori eradication after treatment and the required washout intervals.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: HCC resection selection in compensated cirrhosis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: For the approved favorable compensated-cirrhosis profile, select hospital HPB-surgery referral for hepatic resection evaluation without treating Child-Pugh A status or Milan classification alone as sufficient.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Apply standard Milan criteria to HCC referral
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Apply standard Milan tumor-number, size, macrovascular-invasion, and extrahepatic-disease criteria to recognize when HCC tumor burden supports transplant-center evaluation without treating the criteria as automatic listing.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Emergency CT evaluation after anticoagulated head injury
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Send an anticoagulated adult with mild head injury for emergency evaluation and strongly considered head CT rather than using a usual decision rule to exclude imaging.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Multiphasic MRI characterization of hepatic adenoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select multiphasic liver MRI to characterize a suspected hepatic adenoma while respecting imaging limitations.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Resection planning for hepatic adenoma in men
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer a stable man with a characterized hepatic adenoma for elective resection planning regardless of lesion size.
